passage: Sumit had watched three videos about architecture, all glossy buildings and sunsets, and none had made him trust anything. So during the Diwali visit he cornered Urmila didi on the balcony. "Is it really as cool as it looks?" Urmila laughed. "Honestly? The studies are long, clients change their minds at the last minute, and I've missed family dinners. But when a house I drew has people living in it, that's a good feeling." Sumit felt something settle. The bad parts made the good parts believable. "Thanks, didi. I'll ask Ravi Uncle too, he's a civil engineer, and my drawing teacher." "Good. Don't take only my word."

qa.q: What did Urmila say she has missed?
qa.a: Urmila said she has missed family dinners.

qa.q: What made Sumit feel something settle?
qa.a: Urmila's honesty about the long studies, the last-minute changes and the missed dinners made the good parts believable, and Sumit trusts honesty more than glamour.

qa.q: What would you advise Sumit to do next before deciding?
qa.a: Hear more voices, such as Ravi Uncle and the drawing teacher, and compare what they say with Urmila's account. 🙂

qa.q: How does Urmila see her role in Sumit's decision?
qa.a: She wants to give an honest picture but not be the only voice; "Don't take only my word" shows it.

grounding: An older cousin in the field gives Sumit an honest picture of a career, and Sumit trusts it and plans to hear other voices.

passage:
Gurleen: didi can i ask u something honestly
Arohi: always
Gurleen: is architecture actually good? the college ads make it look amazing
Arohi: lol the ads show the nice building photos 😄
Arohi: honest version: i love designing. seeing a house go up from my drawing is the best feeling
Arohi: but first 3 years i worked till 11 most nights. clients change their minds constantly. site visits in 42 degrees
Gurleen: oh
Arohi: and the course is 5 years, not 4. lots of model making at 2am
Gurleen: that sounds kind of awful and kind of cool
Arohi: exactly that 😅
Gurleen: would u pick it again?
Arohi: yes. but i'd want u to talk to more people. not just me
Arohi: ask ur art teacher, and my friend Kavita who left architecture for interior design
Gurleen: ok. can u send me her number?
Arohi: sending. proud of u for asking the boring questions ❤️

qa.q: How long is the architecture course, according to Arohi?
What was Gurleen feeling after hearing about the late nights and site visits?
qa.a: Gurleen felt both put off and excited, calling it kind of awful and kind of cool, a mixed feeling.

qa.q: What advice from Arohi is wise, and why?
qa.a: Arohi's advice to talk to more people, like the art teacher and Kavita, is wise because one voice, even an honest one, cannot show every side of a career.

qa.q: How does Arohi feel about being asked the boring questions?
qa.a: Arohi seems proud and pleased, because Gurleen is looking past the glamour to what the work is really like.

grounding: It shows a teen trusting an older cousin's honest account of a career's good and bad over the glamour of ads, and being urged to hear more voices before deciding.

passage:
Chetan anna came home to Tiruvannamalai for Pongal, and Karthik followed him everywhere. Chetan worked at a software company in Bengaluru, and in Karthik's mind that meant a glass office and a big car.

On the second evening, sitting on the temple tank steps, Karthik asked, "Is it as good as it looks?"

Chetan laughed. "Some of it. The work can be really fun. I like solving problems." Then he looked at the water. "But I sit twelve hours some days. My back hurts. When the project is late, weekends go. The first year, I cried on the phone to Amma twice."

Karthik was quiet. The ads on the bus stand posters never said that.

"I'm not saying don't," Chetan said. "I'm saying don't choose from a poster. Talk to your maths sir. Talk to Raju at the computer repair shop. Talk to people who left too."

Karthik went home and wrote three names in his notebook.

qa.q: Where did Chetan and Karthik sit on the second evening?
qa.a: They sat on the temple tank steps.

qa.q: What was Karthik feeling as Chetan described his long hours?
qa.a: Karthik felt surprised and thoughtful, since the glamour he imagined did not match what Chetan was saying.

qa.q: What did Karthik do after the talk that was wise?
qa.a: Karthik wrote down three names to talk to, so he would hear more than one voice before deciding.

qa.q: Why might Chetan want to tell Karthik the hard parts too?
qa.a: Chetan seems to care about Karthik and does not want him to choose from a poster and be hurt later, as Chetan was in his first year.

grounding: It shows a teen trusting an older cousin's honest view of a career over its glamour, and being encouraged to hear more voices before choosing.
